name: Spatial Mapping
description:
Spatial mapping records how activities, people, objects or experiences are distributed and connected within a physical environment. Designers may map movement, occupation, interaction, visibility, obstacles, resources or moments of activity.

The resulting representation helps make relationships between behaviour and space visible.
whenToUse: Use spatial mapping when physical arrangement, movement or environmental conditions influence an experience.
steps: Obtain or create a simple plan of the space.
Decide what activities or features will be recorded.
Observe the space over an appropriate period.
Mark locations, movements and events on the map.
Use layers or notation to distinguish different observations.
Compare patterns across times or participants.
Identify spatial constraints and opportunities for further investigation.
lookOutFor: Short observation periods may capture unusual rather than typical patterns.
Mapping people's locations can create privacy concerns.
Avoid assuming that visible movement explains why people behave as they do; combine mapping with other research where necessary.

resources.citation: Zeisel, J. (2006). *Inquiry by Design*, rev. ed. W. W. Norton.
